spec.name: Earnings drift v6
spec.notes: Post-earnings drift on the reported surprise.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.7, annual return 4%, maximum drawdown 2%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.66 to 1.56 (change -0.11).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.66 to -0.30. Changed by strict mode: fields eps_reported.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.64 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.66); it breaks even at 148.3 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.66 against 1.66 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.34 against 1.66 in research, a gap of +1.33.
The best year gives 15% of total P&L (year 9) and calm regimes give 87%; Sharpe is 2.2 in calm and 0.69 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.23, so the claimed 1.70 becomes 1.47 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.76 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.03, 95th percentile 0.47).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 33% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 20% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (pit_replay EX-2, holdout_test EX-5).
